title: Rebuilding the main street in eight months
text: Lancaster rebuilt a stretch of its main street, Lancaster Boulevard, as The BLVD, finished in 2010. Construction took eight months and cost 11.5 million dollars. A 30-foot-wide shaded central walkway, called a ramblas, was inspired by a thoroughfare in Barcelona. The project created more than 800 permanent jobs, along with 1,100 temporary construction jobs.

s1.title: Lancaster, California
s1.quote: In 2010, the city opened The BLVD, a one-mile revitalized stretch of Lancaster Boulevard between 10th Street West and Sierra Highway.

s2.title: Lancaster BLVD
s2.quote: The rapid construction schedule—eight months—and the relatively low price tag of $11.5 million ... A 30-foot-wide shaded central 'ramblas' was added ... inspired by Barcelona's famous thoroughfare ... More than 800 permanent jobs ... 1,100 temporary construction jobs
